svg.aria-label: How VSEARCH builds a consensus sequence from aligned reads
svg.text: 1 · Align every read to the centroid
2 · Count A, C, G, T and gaps in each column
The last 46 columns of a real VSEARCH alignment of six reads (centroid + 5). Every read counts once.
tie: A, C, G, T order → A
One sequence that summarises aligned reads: at each position, the
symbol most reads agree on. Random errors sit at different places
in different reads and are outvoted; differences shared by most
reads stay. With only 2 reads every disagreement is a tie, so a
2-read consensus is little better than one read.
• Each read is aligned pairwise to the centroid; the alignments are
• In every column the most common of A, C, G, T or gap wins.
• Ties: A before C before G before T; a base beats as many gaps.
• A column won by gaps is left out. No quality scores are used.
